newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end easier in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end easier in dull trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower across the board on Monday in stagnant trade with the market seen drifting lower in the absence of fresh demand, dealers said.
The Columbus day holiday in the United States also weighed on market sentiment, the traders said.
"It's a weak market because there are just no fresh orders to pick it up. The amount of tonnages done were very small and not enough to rouse traders' interest," a local rubber dealer said.

Small increases in the price of Japan's rubber markets gave little comfort to local dealers. Tokyo's benchmark March contract inched up 0.3 yen to 134.7 while Kobe's March contract settled at 134.7 after closing last Friday at 134.2.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 122.00-124.00 U.S. cents a kg from 124.25 cents.

November RSS1 was seen at 173.50-175.50 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg from the previous settlement of 175.50 cents. December TSR20 was seen at 170.50-172.50 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.22) a kg against the previous 173.75 cents.
